html:
The Quinault are a Native American people of the Pacific coast of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington, around the Quinault River and Lake Quinault. They spoke a Salishan language, related to the Coast Salish tongues to the east.

They lived in cedar plank houses, travelled in large dugout canoes and lived on salmon, above all the blueback sockeye run of the Quinault River. Neighbours included the Queets, the Quileute to the north and the Chehalis to the south, and they shared in the trade and gift feasts, the potlatch, of the northwest coast. In 1855 and 1856 they signed the Treaty of Olympia, which kept their fishing rights and a reservation at the mouth of the river. The Quinault Indian Nation, based at Taholah, now also includes Queets, Quileute, Chinook and other descendants.
